freeze_attestation: This ordered roster was fixed before any experimental solver, model-auditor, or solver-claim BugBank retrieval call and before any arm outcome existed. Coarse BugBank-topic relevance was intentionally used for selection because this is a targeted stress test, not an outcome-blind cohort.

roster.expected_bugbank_relevance: A finite construction must survive forbidden-subgraph checks and a universal two-edge-coloring argument. Counterexample validation, coloring case splits, and exhaustive-certificate soundness are recurring BugBank-style failure modes.
roster.scope: Only the first K6-free clause; the parenthetical K4-free follow-up is excluded.

roster.expected_bugbank_relevance: The claim combines a graph symmetric-difference metric, a sharp one-edit-per-vertex boundary, witness production, and positive/negative soundness—areas where reduction and edge-edit mistakes can be load-bearing.
Hamiltonicity constructions and robust edge-edit reductions frequently turn on local connectivity, path-splicing, and witness-soundness details represented in BugBank.
roster.scope: Only the subsidiary universal n/c tractability question, not the broad request to determine the full hardness radius.

roster.expected_bugbank_relevance: Dominating-set graph edits require careful threshold preservation, witness construction, and reduction soundness, all plausible matches to BugBank's graph-proof failure modes.
roster.scope: Every fixed c>0, with the instance's dominating-set threshold unchanged.

roster.expected_bugbank_relevance: A proof or counterexample must coordinate separator balance, connectivity after deletion, planarity, and shortest-path claims; these interacting invariants are prone to subtle local proof errors.
roster.scope: One-half balance and two paths shortest in the original graph; the paths may intersect.

roster.expected_bugbank_relevance: Residual-flow, cycle-cancellation, antiparallel-arc, and path-decomposition invariants are classic sources of subtle proof bugs and align with BugBank's flow-related material.
roster.scope: Finite acyclic digraphs, nonzero balance so d_max is defined, exact rational inputs as a narrower bit-model operationalization, and the simultaneous two-sided arc bound.

allowed: Expected relevance to known BugBank subject areas and proof-failure modes.
Exactness and source verifiability of the open statement.
Diversity across constructions, graph editing, separators, and flows.
forbidden: Any BugBank-versus-plain arm result for a selected problem.
Any solver or model-auditor output for a selected problem.
Replacing a problem after observing any experimental outcome.
selection_policy.intent: Deliberately enrich for cases where BugBank might help, to generate hypotheses and stress-test mechanisms rather than estimate performance on an outcome-blind population.
